summary.headline: H1 FY27 GMV rose to INR397 crores (from INR310 crores) while EBITDA stayed a loss of about INR7 crores; FY30 GMV target INR2,100 crores reiterated.
summary.overview: Purple Style Labs (Pernia's Pop-Up Shop) reported H1 FY27 revenue from operations of INR262 crores (vs INR214 crores in H1 FY26) and gross margin of 39% (vs 38%). EBITDA was a loss of about INR7 crores (vs loss of INR5 crores), so growth has not yet converted into operating profit. Operating cash outflow narrowed to INR13 crores (from INR50 crores) and free cash flow was INR19 crores (vs INR72 crores). Management kept the FY30 GMV target of INR2,100 crores, with capex and deposits of roughly INR80-90 crores over 18 months for Delhi and upgrade projects, and said it would not give quarterly guidance.

segments.name: Mumbai
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 GMV of INR105 crores (vs INR77 crores in H1 FY26); FY26 Mumbai GMV was INR205 crores, and management implies INR250 crores+ for FY27 on a 40:60 split.

segments.name: Delhi
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 GMV of INR85 crores; a new 100K sq ft Gen 4 flagship is planned, with Delhi targeted at INR700 crores GMV by FY30.

segments.name: USA
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 GMV of INR64 crores (vs INR42 crores), driven by the New York store opened in March-April 2026; store AOV is above $1,500 vs about $500 online. The New York lease runs to June 27, with a decision due on Q3 call; FY30 US target is INR270 crores.

segments.name: Rest of world / UK
segments.commentary: Covered by a FY30 target of INR180 crores; the London store is planned for upgrade from Gen 1 to Gen 3 with no firm timeline. Management described the store as a 2019 store.

segments.name: Rest of India and India online
segments.commentary: FY30 target of INR450 crores, covering Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, Bangalore, Kolkata, Surat, Chennai, Indore and online; Ahmedabad, Kolkata and Bangalore to be upgraded to Gen 3 format.

guidance_outlook: FY30 GMV target of INR2,100 crores reiterated, with Mumbai INR500 crores, Delhi INR700 crores, rest of India and online INR450 crores, USA INR270 crores and rest of world INR180 crores.
No quarterly guidance; management will stick to the FY30 GMV target. It expects FY27 gross margin above FY26 and H2 GMV about 30% above H1 on the wedding-season pattern.
Cash-basis annual fixed cost base of about INR360-370 crores; profitability requires gross profit to cross that level. Management aims to close most of the gap in FY27 and bridge it fully in FY28.
Revenue-to-GMV conversion guided at about 80% plus or minus 3% on an annual basis (H1 FY27 was about 66%, Q2 about 70%).
Capex plus deposits of about INR80-90 crores (INR75-80 crores in one estimate) over the next 18 months to March 2028 for the five projects.
Interest cost expected to fall in H2 with equity proceeds from the IPO; management expects no operating cash losses in H2 on the H2 seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA at a mature store level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined a store-level or percentage margin, saying costs are largely fixed absent expansion; cash cost base is about INR360-370 crores a year, so incremental GP flows to EBITDA once that threshold is crossed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Delhi store plus three upgrades the only expansion needed for INR2,100 crores GMV by FY30?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Mumbai and USA expansion is done and will drive throughput; London, Ahmedabad, Kolkata and Bangalore are the only remaining upgrades in the plan, with Hyderabad, Indore, Chennai and Surat unchanged. Investment is INR75-80 crores (later INR80-90 crores) over 18 months to March 2028.

qa_highlights.question: How will H2 cash flow and FY27 cash flow look?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 interest was about INR40 crores; management expects no operating cash losses in H2 given H2 seasonality (FY26 H2 revenue INR343 crores vs H1 INR215 crores), with lower interest after IPO equity proceeds, but did not quantify.

qa_highlights.question: Are festive shift and lower destination-wedding travel hurting the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called these minor headwinds given global presence; New York store should offset lower travel from the US. A 15% market growth case still supports INR2,100 crores with 10.5% share.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin trend and when does operating leverage come?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin improved in Q1 and Q2 and FY27 is expected above FY26; the cash break-even is GP of about INR360-370 crores a year, which management aims to close mostly in FY27 and bridge fully in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How is the US store ramping, and what happens at the June 27 lease expiry?
qa_highlights.answer: New York had a learning curve from March-April 2026 but growth has been high since; FY27 US GMV expected around INR150-160 crores (a range of figures was given), and the lease decision will be disclosed on the Q3 call.

qa_highlights.question: How should revenue be derived from the GMV target?
qa_highlights.answer: Use about 80% plus or minus 3% revenue-to-GMV conversion on an annual basis; H1 was about 66% and Q2 about 70% because advances from customers shift revenue into later quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the real jewellery contribution and London store capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Real jewellery is sold from some stores and raises AOV; it is not separately disclosed and will appear as a line item only when sizable (example given: about INR100 crores). London upgrade has no firm timeline and capex is in line with the overall ratio.

capex_capacity: Five projects in progress: new 100K sq ft Gen 4 Delhi flagship, upgrades of Ahmedabad, Kolkata and Bangalore to Gen 3 (each targeted at 10,000-20,000 sq ft, eventually 20,000+), and London upgrade from Gen 1 to Gen 3 with no firm timeline; nothing signed as of the call.

Capex plus deposits estimated at INR80-90 crores over the next 18 months to March 2028 for the five projects (INR75-80 crores in one earlier estimate; INR80-85 crores over 3 years in another answer); management said the 2.5 lakh sq ft existing footprint represents about INR150 crores of capex plus deposits, used as the scaling ratio.

Company currently has about 2.5 lakh sq ft across stores and 14 stores in 11 cities, including London and New York; four large-format stores opened in Mumbai, Delhi and New York in the recent period, with Linking Road and New York opened March-April 2026.
New York store lease runs to June 27 (short lease taken because it was a new geography); management will decide on renewal, renegotiation or exit and will answer on the Q3 call.

Cash fixed cost base of about INR360-370 crores a year; quarterly cash spend about INR85-90 crores; P&L cost base about INR100 crores per quarter, with about INR15 crores a quarter difference from cash basis, mainly ROU depreciation of about INR45 crores vs cash rent of about INR30-31 crores.
demand_pricing: H1 FY27 GMV INR397 crores vs INR310 crores; average order value INR84,000 vs INR69,000; revenue from operations INR262 crores vs INR214 crores.
Mumbai H1 FY27 GMV INR105 crores vs INR77 crores; FY26 Mumbai GMV INR205 crores (INR77 crores H1, INR128 crores H2); management implies INR250 crores+ for FY27 on a 40:60 split and about 30% growth.
Delhi H1 FY27 GMV INR85 crores; FY30 Delhi target INR700 crores with new 100K sq ft Gen 4 flagship.

USA H1 FY27 GMV INR64 crores vs INR42 crores; store AOV above $1,500 vs about $500 online; management declined to split store vs online GMV, citing omnichannel and migration from online to store; pre-store US online GMV was about INR100-120 crores a year.

Market context: top 1,000 designer brands market over INR10,000 crores, expected to reach INR25,000 crores by 2030 per cited industry projection, growing about 20-21%; company's share rose from 2% (2020) to 6% (2025), target 8%+ by 2030. Management said a 15% market growth would still allow INR2,100 crores with 10.5% share.

Designer-wear customer penetration target 25% by 2030 (20% in 2025); wallet share target 34% by 2030 (32% in 2025). Revenue-to-GMV conversion about 80% plus or minus 3% annually; H1 about 66%, Q2 about 70%.

Gross margin improved in Q1 and Q2; management expects FY27 gross margin above FY26. Real jewellery sold from some stores, not inventory-funded; not separately disclosed. Backorders (customer pays 100% upfront, 2-12 week delivery) keep net working capital low: inventory INR196 crores, NWC about INR60 crores.
risks_watch: Profitability: H1 FY27 EBITDA still a loss of about INR7 crores; gross profit must cross roughly INR360-370 crores a year on a cash basis, with the company targeting most of the gap in FY27 and full bridging in FY28.
H2 delivery: management implies H2 GMV about 30% above H1 and attributes a Q2 wedding-shopping delay to Q3 and Q4; any shortfall would weigh on the FY27 view.
New York lease expires June 27 (2027); renewal, renegotiation or exit decision due on the Q3 call. US GMV and store economics remain short-track.
Execution on five projects with nothing signed as of the call; London and Ahmedabad/Kolkata/Bangalore timelines unfixed; Delhi Gen 4 flagship not yet located.

Cash and interest: management expects no operating cash losses in H2 and lower interest after IPO proceeds, but did not quantify; net working capital and inventory (INR196 crores) need to keep falling.
Macro and demand: festive-season shift and lower destination-wedding travel flagged in media; management called them minor but has not quantified.

Data consistency: several transcript corrections are noted (luxury market size, slide references) and some capex figures varied across answers (INR75-80 crores, INR80-85 crores, INR80-90 crores), so the basis should be confirmed.
key_quotes: So what tends to happen, let's say Mumbai stores do a certain number in the first financial year, which is FY27.
So let's say today if my annual expenses are in the range of INR360 crores, INR370 crores on a cash basis, once I cross INR360 crores, INR370 crores of GP, that means we become profitable from there.
So I think so long as we are able to reduce this net working capital going forward it would actually amplify our capital efficiency in this business versus any other platform.
But I think if there is any such headwind due to geopolitical issues, our New York store will compensate for that.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term FY30 GMV target and on Mumbai and US throughput, but cautious and non-committal on quarterly numbers, the New York lease, and the timing of the new projects, repeatedly declining to give quarterly guidance or store-level margins.
